subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): narrow wildcard barrels to explicit used exports

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally make this symbol-level plugin-SDK break before a major release, or preserve the released exports through the normal deprecation/removal window?
rationale: The PR says this was a maintainer-directed contraction, but the checked-in SDK policy explicitly reserves breaking public removals for major-version work; only a maintainer can confirm an intentional exception or require compatibility preservation.

options.title: Preserve compatibility first
options.body: Retain every currently shipped symbol as an explicit compatibility export, add deprecations and replacements, and defer removals to the normal window or next major release.

options.title: Approve a major contract break
options.body: Land the contraction only as an explicitly approved breaking release with migration documentation, release communication, and upgrade proof for representative external plugins.

options.title: Split internal cleanup
options.body: Land only the internal import tightening and genuinely private dead-code deletion now, then handle public export removal in a separately reviewed compatibility change.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility first
recommendation.body: Retain every currently shipped symbol as an explicit compatibility export, add deprecations and replacements, and defer removals to the normal window or next major release.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current contract-reduction series, authored the adjacent windowing change, and is the best-positioned documented maintainer to confirm whether the claimed directive overrides normal SDK compatibility policy.
